lists.name: Grade 3 — Everyday Words
lists.description: High-use words for 8–9 year olds: home, school, friends and feelings. Each word has a kid-friendly definition and a sentence to read aloud.
lists.subject: english

words.definition: A crunchy fruit with red, green or yellow skin that grows on trees
words.example: I packed an apple in my lunch box.

words.definition: Pages with words or pictures, held together inside a cover, that you read
words.example: Mia read a book about sharks before bed.

words.definition: A small furry pet with whiskers that purrs when it is happy
words.example: Our cat naps in the sunny spot by the window.

words.definition: A furry pet that barks, wags its tail and loves to fetch
words.example: The dog ran after the ball and brought it back.

words.definition: A building where a family lives
words.example: Their house has a red door and a big yard.

words.definition: To push off the ground with your legs so your whole body goes up in the air
words.example: Can you jump over the puddle without getting wet?

words.definition: To chew and swallow food
words.example: We eat dinner together at six o'clock.

words.definition: Someone you like, trust and enjoy spending time with
words.example: My friend Sam saved me a seat on the bus.

words.definition: Nice, helpful or done well; the opposite of bad
words.example: You did a good job cleaning up the paint.

words.definition: Feeling glad, the way you feel when you smile or laugh
words.example: Grandpa was happy to see us at the door.

words.definition: Gentle and caring; acting in ways that help others feel good
words.example: Leo is kind to new kids in our class.

words.definition: Making little or no noise
words.example: The library is a quiet place to read.

words.definition: To let someone else use or have part of something that is yours
words.example: Let's share the last slice of pizza.

words.definition: To make happy sounds because something is funny
words.example: The puppy's silly tricks made everyone laugh.

words.definition: Ready to do something scary or hard even when you feel afraid
words.example: The brave firefighter climbed the tall ladder.

words.definition: To take something for a short time and then give it back
words.example: May I borrow your eraser for a minute?

words.definition: Paying close attention so you do not make a mistake or get hurt
words.example: Be careful when you carry the hot soup.

lists.name: Grade 5 — Words for Stories and Life
lists.description: Words 10–11 year olds meet in novels, class discussions and writing prompts, from adventure to opinion.
lists.subject: english

words.definition: Very lovely to look at or listen to
words.example: We watched a beautiful sunset over the lake.

words.definition: Liked the most, more than all the others
words.example: Blue is my favorite color.

words.definition: Mattering a lot; something you should pay attention to
words.example: Sleep is important for a growing body.

words.definition: To tell what someone or something is like using words
words.example: Can you describe the monster in your dream?

words.definition: To travel around a place to find out what it is like
words.example: We used a map to explore the old castle.

words.definition: An exciting trip or experience full of new things, sometimes with a little danger
words.example: Camping in the mountains was a real adventure.

words.definition: To do something fun and special because of an important day or event
words.example: We celebrate my sister's birthday with a picnic.

words.definition: To find or learn something for the first time
words.example: Divers hope to discover new kinds of fish.

words.definition: Feeling thankful when someone helps you or gives you something
words.example: I was grateful when a classmate found my lost jacket.

words.definition: The study of things that happened in the past
words.example: In history class we learned how the pyramids were built.

words.definition: A long trip from one place to another
words.example: The journey across the ocean took two weeks.

words.definition: Wanting to know or learn about something
words.example: The curious kitten sniffed every box in the room.

words.definition: The air, water, land, plants and animals around us that living things need
words.example: Picking up litter helps protect the environment.

words.definition: Something hard that tests how strong, smart or skillful you are
words.example: Learning the guitar is a fun challenge.

words.definition: What you think or believe about something, which others may not agree with
words.example: In my opinion, summer is the best season.

words.definition: The answer to a problem or a way to fix it
words.example: Our team found a solution to the puzzle in five minutes.

words.definition: Able to wait calmly without getting upset
words.example: Please be patient while the cookies bake.

lists.name: Grade 7 — Academic Words for Every Subject
lists.description: The thinking words middle schoolers see in science labs, essays and test questions: analyze, infer, evaluate and more.
lists.subject: english

words.definition: To share ideas or feelings by talking, writing, signing or using gestures
words.example: Dolphins communicate with clicks and whistles.

words.definition: Tools, machines and inventions people create with science to solve problems
words.example: New technology lets doctors see inside the body without surgery.

words.definition: To look at two or more things to see how they are alike and different
words.example: Compare the two maps and list three changes.

words.definition: To say what you think will happen before it happens
words.example: Can you predict how the story will end?

words.definition: To study something closely, piece by piece, to understand how it works or why it happened
words.example: Scientists analyze water samples to check for pollution.

words.definition: To show how something works or prove that something is true
words.example: The coach will demonstrate the correct way to serve.

words.definition: To search for facts to find out what happened or how something works
words.example: The detective came to investigate the missing painting.

words.definition: To retell the main ideas in a few words, leaving out small details
words.example: Summarize the chapter in three sentences.

words.definition: Facts or objects that show whether something is true
words.example: Footprints in the mud were evidence that a deer had passed.

words.definition: To decide something is true after thinking about all the facts
words.example: From the clues, we can conclude that the butler is innocent.

words.definition: The order in which events or steps happen
words.example: Put the pictures in the right sequence to tell the story.

words.definition: To judge how good, useful or correct something is after looking at it carefully
words.example: Use the checklist to evaluate your partner's essay.

words.definition: A possible explanation that you can test with an experiment
words.example: Our hypothesis was that plants grow faster with music.

words.definition: The way a person sees a situation, shaped by who they are and what they have lived through
words.example: The story is told from the perspective of the dog.

words.definition: Large or important enough to make a real difference
words.example: There was a significant drop in temperature overnight.

words.definition: To figure out something that is not said directly, using clues and what you already know
words.example: From his muddy boots, we can infer that Max walked through the field.

words.definition: Closely connected to the topic you are talking about
words.example: Only include facts that are relevant to your argument.

lists.name: Grade 2 — Animals and Where They Live
lists.description: Life-science words for 7–8 year olds: animal homes, body coverings and how animals survive the seasons.
lists.subject: science

words.definition: A cozy home birds build from twigs, grass and mud to hold their eggs
words.example: Two robins built a nest in our apple tree.

words.definition: A small, still body of water, smaller than a lake
words.example: Frogs and ducks live at the pond behind our school.

words.definition: A large area covered with many trees
words.example: Bears, deer and owls live in the forest.

words.definition: The huge body of salt water that covers most of Earth
words.example: Whales swim thousands of miles across the ocean.

words.definition: The thick, soft hair that covers many animals
words.example: A polar bear's thick fur keeps it warm on the ice.

words.definition: A hole or tunnel in the ground that an animal digs to live in
words.example: The rabbit hid in its burrow when the fox came near.

words.definition: A very dry place that gets almost no rain
words.example: Camels can walk for days across the desert.

words.definition: The soft, light parts covering a bird's body that help it fly and stay warm
words.example: The parrot has bright green feathers.

words.definition: Small, hard, flat pieces that cover the skin of fish and snakes
words.example: The fish's silver scales shimmered in the sunlight.

words.definition: A large group of animals, like cows or elephants, that live and move together
words.example: A herd of zebras crossed the river.

words.definition: A baby frog that lives in water and swims with its tail
words.example: The tadpole will slowly grow legs and lose its tail.

words.definition: A place that keeps you safe from bad weather or danger
words.example: The cave gave the bats shelter from the storm.

words.definition: The natural home where a plant or animal finds the food, water and shelter it needs
words.example: A coral reef is a habitat for colorful fish.

words.definition: To sleep deeply through the cold winter months
words.example: Some bears hibernate until spring comes.

words.definition: An animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal
words.example: Mice are prey for owls and hawks.

words.definition: To travel far away when the seasons change, usually to find food or warmth
words.example: Geese migrate south every fall.

lists.name: Grade 3 — Weather and Seasons
lists.description: Earth-science words for talking about the sky, storms and the four seasons, plus a few forecast words for the stretch tier.
lists.subject: science

words.definition: What the air outside is like right now: sunny, rainy, windy, hot or cold
words.example: The weather was perfect for flying kites.

words.definition: One of the four parts of the year: spring, summer, fall and winter
words.example: Spring is the season when flowers bloom.

words.definition: A white or gray shape in the sky made of tiny drops of water
words.example: A dark cloud covered the sun.

words.definition: An arch of colors in the sky when sunlight shines through raindrops
words.example: After the rain, a rainbow stretched over the hills.

words.definition: A small pool of water on the ground after it rains
words.example: My little brother stomped in every puddle.

words.definition: The loud booming sound you hear after lightning flashes
words.example: The thunder was so loud that the windows shook.

words.definition: A bright flash of electricity in the sky during a storm
words.example: We counted the seconds between the lightning and the boom.

words.definition: A light, gentle wind
words.example: A cool breeze blew through the open window.

words.definition: To turn hard and icy because it is very cold
words.example: Ponds freeze in the middle of winter.

words.definition: To turn from a solid into a liquid as it warms up
words.example: The snowman began to melt in the sun.

words.definition: The season after summer, when leaves change color and drop; also called fall
words.example: In autumn, we rake big piles of leaves.

words.definition: To shake a little because you are cold or scared
words.example: We started to shiver while waiting for the bus in the snow.

words.definition: A report that says what the weather will probably be like soon
words.example: The forecast says it will snow tomorrow.

words.definition: How hot or cold something is, measured with a thermometer
words.example: The temperature dropped quickly after sunset.

words.definition: A long time with little or no rain, when the land becomes very dry
words.example: During the drought, the farmers' crops dried up.

words.definition: Damp and sticky because there is a lot of water in the air
words.example: It was so humid that my shirt stuck to my back.

lists.name: Grade 4 — Feelings and Character
lists.description: Social-emotional vocabulary for naming feelings precisely and describing character traits in stories and in class.
lists.subject: general

words.definition: Very happy and eager about something that is going to happen
words.example: I was too excited to sleep the night before the trip.

words.definition: Worried or a little scared about something
words.example: Ava felt nervous before her piano recital.

words.definition: Feeling good about something you or someone close to you did well
words.example: Dad was proud when I finished the race.

words.definition: Always telling the truth and never cheating or stealing
words.example: Thank you for being honest about the broken vase.

words.definition: Peaceful and not upset or worried
words.example: Take a deep breath and stay calm.

words.definition: Upset because someone has something you want
words.example: He felt jealous when his friend got a new bike.

words.definition: Sad because you are alone or feel that nobody is with you
words.example: On her first day at a new school, Lily felt lonely.

words.definition: Feeling silly or shy because others saw you make a mistake
words.example: I was embarrassed when I tripped on stage.

words.definition: Sure that you can do something well
words.example: After lots of practice, she felt confident about the test.

words.definition: Happy to give or share what you have with others
words.example: Our generous neighbor gave us tomatoes from her garden.

words.definition: In a bad mood and easily annoyed
words.example: I'm always grumpy when I wake up too early.

words.definition: Happy, bright and full of good spirits
words.example: The cheerful bus driver greets every child by name.

words.definition: Treating someone as important and caring about their feelings and ideas
words.example: We show respect by listening when others speak.

words.definition: Annoyed and upset because something is not working the way you want
words.example: I got frustrated when my kite kept crashing.

words.definition: Doing what you are supposed to do, so others can count on you
words.example: Being responsible means feeding the fish every day.

words.definition: Not giving up, even when something is very hard
words.example: The determined climber reached the top of the mountain.

words.definition: Understanding how someone else feels, as if you were in their place
words.example: Showing empathy can make a sad friend feel less alone.

lists.name: Grade 3 — Math Words
lists.description: The words of operations, shapes and measurement that 3rd graders need to read and explain math problems.
lists.subject: math

words.definition: To put numbers together to find how many there are in all
words.example: If you add 4 and 5, you get 9.

words.definition: Exactly the same in amount or size
words.example: Two plus two is equal to four.

words.definition: The answer you get when you add numbers
words.example: The sum of 7 and 8 is 15.

words.definition: The outline or form of something, like a circle or a square
words.example: A stop sign has the shape of an octagon.

words.definition: A perfectly round flat figure with no corners
words.example: We sat in a circle on the rug.

words.definition: To take one number away from another
words.example: Subtract 3 from 10 to find out how many cookies are left.

words.definition: To find the total of equal groups quickly, like 3 groups of 4 making 12
words.example: Multiply 6 by 2 to find how many eggs are in two rows.

words.definition: To split an amount into equal groups
words.example: Divide 12 apples among 4 friends, and each gets 3.

words.definition: A flat figure with three straight sides and three corners
words.example: A slice of pizza looks like a triangle.

words.definition: To find the size, length or amount of something
words.example: Use a ruler to measure your pencil.

words.definition: Shapes, numbers or colors that repeat in a regular way
words.example: Red, blue, red, blue is a simple pattern.

words.definition: A number that can be split into two equal groups, like 2, 4 or 6
words.example: Eight is an even number.

words.definition: The answer you get when you take one number away from another
words.example: The difference between 9 and 4 is 5.

words.definition: A number that names part of a whole, like one half or three quarters
words.example: One half is the fraction you get when you cut a pie into two equal parts.

words.definition: A smart guess about an amount, made without counting exactly
words.example: My estimate is that there are 50 marbles in the jar.

words.definition: Any one of the ten symbols 0 to 9 used to write numbers
words.example: The digit in the tens place of 507 is zero.

lists.name: Grade 6 — Earth and Space
lists.description: Astronomy words for the solar system unit: planets, gravity, eclipses and the tools we use to study the sky.
lists.subject: science

words.definition: A huge round object in space that travels around a star
words.example: Mars is the planet known for its red color.

words.definition: A tool that makes faraway objects, like stars, look bigger and closer
words.example: Through the telescope, we could see the rings of Saturn.

words.definition: A person trained to travel and work in space
words.example: The astronaut floated inside the space station.

words.definition: Having to do with the Sun
words.example: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity.

words.definition: Having to do with the Moon
words.example: A lunar month is about 29 days long.

words.definition: To travel in a curved path around a planet or star; also the path itself
words.example: The Moon takes about a month to orbit Earth.

words.definition: The invisible pull that draws objects toward each other and keeps our feet on the ground
words.example: Gravity makes a dropped apple fall to the ground.

words.definition: A giant group of billions of stars held together in space
words.example: Our solar system is part of a galaxy called the Milky Way.

words.definition: A ball of ice and dust that grows a glowing tail when it passes near the Sun
words.example: People could see the comet without a telescope.

words.definition: A bowl-shaped hole made when a rock from space crashes into a surface
words.example: A meteorite left a deep crater in the desert.

words.definition: To spin around a center line, like a top
words.example: Earth takes about 24 hours to rotate once.

words.definition: A space rock that burns up in Earth's air as a streak of light; also called a shooting star
words.example: We made a wish when we saw a meteor.

words.definition: The layer of gases that surrounds a planet
words.example: Earth's atmosphere protects us from harmful rays.

words.definition: When one object in space blocks the light of another, as when the Moon hides the Sun
words.example: During the eclipse, the sky turned dark at noon.

words.definition: An object that travels around a planet, like the Moon or a machine sent into space
words.example: A weather satellite takes pictures of clouds from space.

words.definition: An imaginary line through the middle of a planet that it spins around
words.example: Earth is tilted on its axis, which gives us seasons.

lists.name: Grade 8 — Government and Citizenship
lists.description: Civics vocabulary for how laws are made, how leaders are chosen and what rights and duties citizens share.
lists.subject: history

words.definition: A person who legally belongs to a country and has its rights and duties
words.example: Every citizen has the right to a fair trial.

words.definition: To make an official choice, for example by marking a ballot
words.example: Students will vote for a class president on Friday.

words.definition: An organized event where people cast ballots to choose leaders
words.example: The election will be held in November.

words.definition: A rule made by a government that everyone must follow
words.example: There is a law that drivers must wear seat belts.

words.definition: Being able to act, speak and think without being controlled by others
words.example: Freedom of speech lets people share their opinions.

words.definition: A system of government in which people choose their leaders by voting
words.example: In a democracy, every adult citizen can vote.

words.definition: Freedoms and protections that every person should have
words.example: Children have rights, such as going to school and being safe.

words.definition: Fair treatment for everyone, especially under the law
words.example: The marchers carried signs calling for justice.

words.definition: A discussion in which people give reasons for different sides of an issue
words.example: The candidates held a debate on television.

words.definition: Money people and businesses pay to the government to fund things like schools and roads
words.example: A sales tax is added to the price of many things you buy.

words.definition: A person who is trying to be chosen in an election
words.example: Each candidate gave a short speech.

words.definition: To show publicly that you strongly disagree with something
words.example: Hundreds of students gathered to protest peacefully.

words.definition: The written set of basic laws that explains how a country is governed
words.example: The constitution protects freedom of speech.

words.definition: The group of elected people who make the laws for a country or state
words.example: The legislature passed a new law about clean water.

words.definition: An official change or addition to a law or a constitution
words.example: The amendment gave women the right to vote.

words.definition: The power of a leader to reject a law that lawmakers have passed
words.example: The president used a veto to block the bill.

lists.name: Grade 10 — Words for Building an Argument
lists.description: The vocabulary of debate, persuasive essays and source analysis for 15–16 year olds. Definitions are precise enough to grade against, and examples come from real classroom tasks.
lists.subject: english

words.definition: A statement that something is true, which you then have to back up with reasons and evidence
words.example: Her claim was that school should start an hour later.

words.definition: An explanation of why something is true or why someone acts a certain way
words.example: Give one reason the city should build more bike lanes.

words.definition: A book, article, person or website that information comes from
words.example: Always check who wrote a source before you trust it.

words.definition: The people who will read, hear or watch what you create
words.example: Choose words that suit your audience, whether it is classmates or the city council.

words.definition: The main point an essay sets out to prove, usually stated in the introduction
words.example: Your thesis should fit in one clear sentence.

words.definition: To get someone to believe or do something by giving them good reasons
words.example: The ad tried to persuade teens to drink more water.

words.definition: A one-sided leaning that stops a person or source from treating all sides fairly
words.example: The article showed bias because it quoted only one side.

words.definition: Trustworthy and believable, usually because of expertise or strong evidence
words.example: A peer-reviewed study is more credible than an anonymous post.

words.definition: Clear, step-by-step reasoning in which each idea follows from the one before
words.example: The logic of his argument broke down in the second paragraph.

words.definition: Built on sound reasoning, so the conclusion really follows from the reasons
words.example: That is a valid point, but it does not answer the main question.

words.definition: Based on facts rather than personal feelings
words.example: A news report should be objective, not full of the writer's opinions.

words.definition: An idea that an argument accepts as true and builds on
words.example: The premise of the debate was that homework helps students learn.

words.definition: An argument against your claim, which a strong essay names and then answers
words.example: Address the counterclaim that uniforms limit self-expression.

words.definition: A reply that shows why an opposing argument is wrong or weak
words.example: In her rebuttal, Maya pointed out that the survey asked only ten people.

words.definition: A mistake in reasoning that makes an argument seem convincing when it is not
words.example: Saying everyone does it is a fallacy, not evidence.

words.definition: To admit that part of the other side's argument is true
words.example: Good debaters concede small points to win bigger ones.

lists.name: כיתה ג׳ — אנגלית: מילים מבית הספר
lists.description: מילים באנגלית לתלמידים דוברי עברית: הגדרה בעברית ומשפט לדוגמה באנגלית. משחקים על לוח באנגלית.
lists.subject: english

words.definition: בית ספר — המקום שבו לומדים עם מורים וחברים לכיתה
words.example: I walk to school with my brother.

words.definition: מורה — האדם שמלמד אותנו בכיתה
words.example: Our teacher reads us a story every Friday.

words.definition: עיפרון — כלי כתיבה שאפשר למחוק את מה שכותבים בו
words.example: Can I use your pencil?

words.definition: משפחה — ההורים, האחים והאחיות, הסבים והסבתות
words.example: My family eats dinner together.

words.definition: מים — הנוזל השקוף שאנחנו שותים כשאנחנו צמאים
words.example: Drink some water after you run.

words.definition: לשחק — לעשות משהו בשביל הכיף, למשל משחק או ספורט
words.example: Let's play soccer at recess.

words.definition: תלמיד או תלמידה — מי שלומד בבית הספר
words.example: There is a new student in my class.

words.definition: מחברת — דפים כרוכים יחד שכותבים בהם
words.example: Write the new words in your notebook.

words.definition: אוכל — מה שאוכלים כדי לגדול ולקבל כוח
words.example: Pizza is my favorite food.

words.definition: לקרוא — להסתכל על מילים כתובות ולהבין אותן
words.example: I like to read comics in bed.

words.definition: לכתוב — לרשום אותיות ומילים על דף או במחשב
words.example: Please write your name at the top.

words.definition: סרגל — כלי ישר למדידה ולציור קווים
words.example: Use a ruler to draw a straight line.

words.definition: ארוחת צהריים — הארוחה שאוכלים באמצע היום
words.example: We eat lunch at twelve o'clock.

words.definition: מחק — חפץ קטן שמוחק סימני עיפרון
words.example: My eraser fell under the desk.

words.definition: שיעורי בית — משימות שעושים בבית אחרי הלימודים
words.example: I finish my homework before I watch TV.

words.definition: כיתה — החדר שבו לומדים
words.example: Our classroom has big windows.
